text:
git add src/ir_lower/program/spl_discovery.rs tests/codegen/spl/dynamic_method_name.rs && git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(spl): a method call through a PARENT-typed receiver segfaulted on the subclass

`function walk(SplFileObject $o) { $o->eof(); }` called with an `SplTempFileObject` died
with SIGSEGV. Adding an unrelated `$temp->eof()` anywhere else in the same program made it
work, which is what said the gap was EMISSION and not dispatch: the vtable slot was null
because nothing had lowered that class's body.

The discovery pass reads a method name off the call and climbs from the receiver's static
type to the class that DECLARES it. That is the right answer for the type and the wrong one
for the object in it — a virtual call lands on whatever the receiver actually holds, and a
subclass that OVERRIDES the method needs its own slot filled.

Bounded by what the program CONSTRUCTS, because a virtual call can only land on a class
something instantiated: a program that builds no SPL subclass walks its class table and
emits nothing.

The two shapes are one bug seen twice — this is the same emission list that answered
`callable array did not resolve to an invokable target` for `$obj->$name()`. A name the
program never spells statically has no body, and the failure it produces depends only on
how the call reaches the missing slot.
